title: Software Engineer Salary Japan 2026: Tokyo Pay Guide
metaDescription: Software engineer salary Japan 2026: Tokyo average 7.2-9.5M yen, entry 4-7M, senior 10-17M. See gaishikei premiums, top employers and hiring tips.
headline: Software Engineer Salary in Japan 2026: Tokyo Pay Guide

sections.content:
Tokyo dominates Japan's software engineering pay landscape in 2026. Glassdoor data from over three thousand submissions puts the average Tokyo software engineer salary at approximately 7.2 million yen per year, with the typical range running from 5.5 million at the 25th percentile to 10.29 million at the 75th percentile.

Other benchmarks run higher: Levels.fyi reports average total compensation of 8.5 million yen in the Greater Tokyo Area, and CareerCheck reports a median of 9.5 million yen. For practical purposes, most engineers in Tokyo earn between 7.2 and 9.5 million yen, with senior and specialized roles going much higher.
sections.title: Average Software Engineer Salary in Tokyo for 2026

sections.content:
Entry-level engineers with zero to two years earn between 4 and 7 million yen per year, with new graduates at traditional domestic firms near the bottom. Mid-level engineers with three to six years earn 7 to 12 million yen, which covers the Tokyo average band.

Senior engineers with seven or more years earn 10 to 17 million yen, while staff and principal engineers at multinational firms earn 15 to 25 million yen. Top earners in the 90th percentile report up to 13.15 million yen across the broader market.
sections.title: Salary by Experience Level

sections.content:
International-headquartered companies pay a large premium in Japan: developers at gaishikei firms report median pay about 35 percent higher than peers at domestic companies. Google Tokyo, for example, reports median compensation around 24.4 million yen for levels L3 to L6.

The premium reflects global salary bands, equity grants and English-language workplaces. Domestic giants and startups are catching up, but the gap remains the single biggest lever an engineer in Japan can pull when changing jobs.
sections.title: Gaishikei vs Domestic Firms

sections.content:
Foreign engineers typically need a valid work visa, most commonly the Engineer, Specialist in Humanities and International Services status, which requires a relevant degree or ten years of experience. Many Tokyo tech firms now hire entirely in English, though Japanese ability opens far more options and speeds up promotions.

Building skills in short supply, such as AI engineering, platform engineering or security, strengthens both visa sponsorship chances and salary offers. Contributing to open source and maintaining a strong GitHub profile also helps, since Japanese hiring managers weigh demonstrable output heavily.
